Please review the following manuscript written by my collaborator.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-qwczo26o/call-1a9cd5be98d74967bfb3160b89901843/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la manuscript.pdf .agents && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, shutil
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
    s=importlib.util.find_spec(name)
    print(name, s.origin if s else None)
for name in ['pdftotext','pdftoppm','pdfinfo','gs','python3']:
    print(name,shutil.which(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('pages',len(reader.pages))
print('metadata',reader.metadata)
for i,page in enumerate(reader.pages):
    text=page.extract_text()
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'PAGE {i+1}\\n'+page.extract_text() for i,page in enumerate(reader.pages)))
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

strengths: Addresses an important efficiency problem in multimodal models through a simple combination of CLIP attention-based token selection and key-based merging. Reusing existing representations avoids introducing a separate learned selector and permits training-free use.

Table 1 reports substantial compression, from 576 to approximately 40 visual tokens, across six benchmarks and two LLaVA-1.5 model sizes. Preserving ScienceQA and POPE performance relatively well after fine-tuning is a useful empirical finding.

The ablations provide evidence that both informed selection and merging help. Training-free TextVQA reaches 54.00 versus 47.96 for the best spatial-sampling baseline in Table 3; adding token supplementation raises MME from 1221.6 to 1350.3 in Table 4.
The high-level pipeline is understandable, relevant foundational methods and datasets are credited, and the limitations section appropriately acknowledges lossy compression and restricted validation.
weaknesses: The comparisons do not establish the advantage of the proposed adaptive mechanism over strong alternatives. Table 3 mainly compares against selecting the first 40 tokens and fixed spatial grids. Fixed-budget attention top-k with the same merging stage and an adaptation of the cited token-merging method are important missing controls. Matched-budget comparisons and accuracy–cost curves are needed to establish whether IQR-based allocation improves the tradeoff beyond straightforward existing techniques.

Practical acceleration remains unverified. Table 2 supplies roofline estimates for LLM prefill under an assumed prompt length and average visual-token count. There are no measured end-to-end latency or peak-memory results incorporating vision encoding, selection/merging overhead, and autoregressive decoding. These omissions matter for an efficiency contribution, particularly with variable token counts and batching.

The headline performance characterization understates substantial task-dependent losses. In Table 1, VQAv2 drops from 78.5 to 72.0 for 7B and from 80.0 to 72.8 for 13B; 7B MME falls from 1510.7 to 1350.3, and 13B MMBench from 67.7 to 62.3. Such losses may be acceptable for aggressive compression, but the broad claim of preserving capabilities needs qualification and stronger characterization of the operating tradeoff.

Important algorithmic and implementation details prevent confident reproduction. Algorithm 1 appears to exclude the retained center from its neighbors and overwrite it with an unnormalized weighted sum, whereas the surrounding description emphasizes supplementing retained tokens through weighted averaging. The neighbor count k, attention-head aggregation, treatment of overlapping clusters, and LoRA hyperparameters are unspecified. These choices can materially change the resulting representations and performance.

The strongest results depend substantially on additional fine-tuning, but the corresponding controls are incomplete. Section 4.1 adds an instruction-tuning epoch, and Table 5 shows POPE improving from 76.2 to 86.3 through adaptation. The manuscript does not report a full-token control receiving the same additional training or equally fine-tuned alternative reduction methods; Table 4 also leaves its training protocol unclear. Consequently, the benefits attributable specifically to pruning and merging remain insufficiently isolated.
